The queue row Q189 and the note N-s3c-5 were read whole, with `checks/M0-c-05-s3.md` (3).

**What the round did** (`prune.ts:155 – 169`). After `splitThrough` has placed the cut, the trim reads the cut vertex
the kernel committed. Where that vertex is the street's end, the exit lies on the street's last segment, and the
street's `to` is an `end` row whose one arm is the street, the trim takes the new junction row back off the vertex, sets
`st.way.provisional` and `st.provisional` false, `st.ends` 'dead' and `st.meets` null, and goes on to the next street.
It asks `removeEdges` for no stretch, counts no refusal, adds no `trimmed` entry and does not advance `jN`. Any other
shape takes the old path.

**Against the trim's success path** (`prune.ts:176 – 195`, read field by field). A trimmed street ends with both
`provisional` flags false, `ends` 'dead', `meets` null, and `to` on an `end` row whose one arm is the street. The
untrimmed street gets the same four flags and keeps its own row of that shape (`junction:121` for `way:65`: kind `end`,
arms `['way:65']`, `generated(0)`). The builder's table in 'Hardening round S4' says the same. CONFIRMED (read; and the
hit probe below prints the street and its row).

**The session's reading differs from the code in one point, and the fix follows the code.** Q189 reads the cut as the
first exit "rounded to the lattice". The fix does not compare the lattice exit with the end; it compares the vertex the
kernel committed. The hand cases show why: an exit 2 cm or 26 cm short of the end still lands on the end vertex (the
kernel's placement attracts a foot to an endpoint within `attractCm`), and the reverted trim counts `E_DEGENERATE`
there too (M1: all three hand cases red). The fix covers the class the finding describes. Not a contract change.

**Why the old code refused.** `kernel/src/tx/chains.ts:102`: a stretch whose `from` and `to` are the same vertex is
`E_DEGENERATE` `stretch`, always. So every firing of the new branch is a run in which the old trim counted
`E_DEGENERATE`; a run whose before-image counts none cannot be moved by the fix.

## (3) New findings (blocker rule)

No gate exits non-zero for a reason of the item's; no interface or test id is missing; no stub or shortcut stands on
an honest path; no wrong result on an honest input was met in 404 runs and the hand cases; no clean-room breach; no
path outside `plat/`. One blocker by the mutation rule, and three notes rows.

### B-1 (M8, notes id N-s4c-1) — a junction id burnt by the trim's new branch moves S5's root and no test sees it

**The mutant.** `jN += 1;` added inside the "nothing to trim" branch (`prune.ts:163 – 168`), before its `continue`.
It is a natural edit, not a contrived one: the success path below advances `jN` at `:176`, and a tidy-up that moves
the increment up beside `newEnd` (`:147`), where the id is named, is this mutant.

**It survives.** `trim.test.ts`, whole file, under M8: *Test Files 1 passed (1)*, *Tests 7 passed (7)*, exit 0
(`m8-trim.log`). The run pins read the batch's other trims and prunes by count (13 / 11, 9 / 9) and each hand case
holds one street, so a renumbered row passes.

**It is not equivalent.** The seat's hit probe under M8 (`hit-m8.log`, `out/hit-m8/hit.jsonl`) against the tree
(`out/hit-after`):

| run | S5 root, the tree | S5 root, M8 | what moved |
|---|---|---|---|
| site fixture 2 000 / 160, seed 5, reroll 0 (the file's first run pin) | `89f45edf09968b337de070c362f45678` | `48322b0b5c58173b0f8c28a9861020da` | the next trim's (`way:70`'s) `end` row is `junction:159` in place of `junction:158`; the record's normalised digest moves too (`cc3fce8d…` → `155bbbd2…`) |
| CITY 2 500 / 220, seed 8, `{ S5: 1 }` (the file's second run pin) | `73779461c698d3efba38c0f6afd20241` | `f64e4dac15dfe578685c9d03e9fa5f3f` | `way:83`'s new `end` row is `junction:191` for `junction:190`; normalised digest `6dd59f55…` → `39b7044e…` |
| CITY 2 500 / 220, seed 4, `{ S5: 1 }` | `87317a1a1e26bd0567e9eb7f1c2358ff` | the same | no trim follows the street in that batch |

So on two registered fixture frames — honest inputs, and the very runs the round's test pins — M8 changes a
seed-to-output digest with every test of the item green.

**Why it is a blocker and not a note.** (a) The promise is stated, and by this round: the session's line for
N-s3c-5 ("A DECLARED SHIFT, and it must move NOTHING ELSE … any other move FAILS"; among the pins, "the batch's other
trims and prunes as before"), C-0496 (1) ("no `trimmed` entry, `jN` not advanced"), whose last column names
`trim.test.ts` as the test that holds the row, the builder's field-by-field table ("`jN` … not advanced, so no later
row of the batch is renumbered") and the test's header. Of the nine rows that table lists, eight have a pin
or are equivalent (M2 – M7, M9, M10, M12 and the hand cases' `to`, row list and points); `jN` is the one that has
none. (b) The branch and the clause are this round's; nothing here predates it. (c) The brief: "a survivor on a
stated promise you do not find equivalent stays a BLOCKER". This flow's closing checks have read that clause the same
way where the code was right and only the pin was missing (`checks/M0-a-11-s1.md`, M13; `checks/M0-a-09-s9.md`), and
recorded a survivor as a hardening row where it fell outside the round's lines (`checks/M0-a-06-s4.md`). M8 falls
inside them. (d) N-45 puts seed-to-output laws among the things fixed now. The tree's result is right today —
the seat's before / after shows the roots equal on every run the branch fires in — so the blocker is the missing pin,
not the trim.
